extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and advocates (Ohio) submitting public comments to government agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for members of the public on composing effective public comments to government bodies (rulemaking, boards, agencies), emphasizing personal testimony, brevity, professional tone, and outreach to others. Framed by ACLU of Ohio for statewide civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share personal stories
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you have a personal story, share it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal stories humanize the issue and help officials understand its importance; use identifying phrases such as "As a teacher" or "As a parent."

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it concise
rubrics_metrics.description: While there are no strict length requirements, brevity is encouraged to maintain focus and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a focused, succinct comment so your main points are clear and memorable; avoid unnecessary length though formal limits may not be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain respect / professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: "Overtly negative language may diminish your credibility and undermine your message."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format comments professionally (for example, as a letter), avoid editorializing and overtly negative or hostile language to preserve credibility and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage others to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Share information with people in your network who might also provide valuable input to the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify impact by prompting friends, colleagues, and community members to submit their own comments if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anyone can submit — accessibility of commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can submit public comment—no special credentials required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are welcomed at various government levels statewide (ACLU of Ohio emphasizes accessibility); lack of formal status or credentials is not a barrier to participation.
